context_requirements: Expression of histamine receptors (HRH1/HRH2/HRH3/HRH4) on the cancer cell
Histamine-dependent autocrine/paracrine survival or proliferative signaling
Intact apoptotic machinery, particularly wild-type TP53 for the strongest response
Sufficient intracellular concentration of the antagonist (some effects are off-target and concentration-dependent)
falsifiers: No consistent transcriptional response across any of the nine cell lines at 6 h or 24 h
Absence of proliferation_down or apoptosis signatures at 24 h in MCF7 despite reported TP53-dependent apoptosis
Lack of any dose-dependent or time-dependent changes in histamine-receptor-expressing lines
Predominant upregulation of proliferation genes rather than downregulation

evidence.supports: H1 antagonist diphenhydramine induces apoptosis in T-ALL lines, suggesting H1 antagonism can trigger cell death
Desloratadine induces TP53-dependent apoptosis in MCF-7 breast cancer cells with upregulation of TP53, FAS, BAX
Ebastine, an H1 antagonist, exerts antitumor activity via AMPK/ULK1-dependent autophagy and apoptosis in osteosarcoma
Loratadine, an H1 antagonist, inhibits histamine-induced fibroblast proliferation and modulates apoptosis markers
Histamine receptor expression varies across hematological cancer lines and modulates survival/apoptosis markers
